262: 6.Marquise de Cat
263: 
264: 6.1Overview
265: 
266: The Marquise de Cat occupies the Woodland and wants to turn it into an industrial and military powerhouse. Each time the Marquise builds one of her buildings—a workshop, sawmill, or recruiter—she scores victory points. The more of the same building she has on the map, the more points she scores. However, to fuel ongoing construction, the Marquise must maintain and protect a strong, interconnected economy of wood.
267: 
268: **Q:**What happens if all of my pieces are removed from the map?
269: 
270: **A:**Unfortunately, you're probably out of the game. However, if the Riverfolk Company or hirelings are in play, you can build a building again if you rule a clearing. Either way, if this happens, the game will likely end at a moment's notice!
271: 
272: 6.2Faction Rules and Abilities
273: 
274: 6.2.1 Crafting.The Marquise crafts during Daylight by activating workshops.
275: 
276: 6.2.2 The Keep.The Marquise can place pieces in the clearing with the keep token, and other players cannot. *(Pieces may be moved into it. If the keep is removed, there is no way to place it on the map again.)*
277: 
278: **Q:**A rule uses a specific term or action. Does it also include another, closely related term or action?
279: 
280: **A:**Nope! Assume we mean only the original term and not any related terms. For example, the terms move and place are different, which is an important distinction in rules such as The Keep.
281: 
282: **Q:**Can someone move a piece into the clearing with my keep?
283: 
284: **A:**Yes! "Place" is a different keyword from "move."
285: 
286: **Q:**Can the Marquise place hirelings at the Keep?
287: 
288: **A:**Yes!
289: 
290: **Q:**Can I revolt in the clearing with the keep token?
291: 
292: **A:**Nope! You would have to place a sympathy token first, which you can't do because of the Marquise's special ability The Keep.
293: 
294: 6.2.3 Field Hospitals.Whenever any number of Marquise warriors are removed from a clearing, the Marquise may spend a card matching that clearing to place those warriors in the clearing with the keep token instead of the Marquise's supply.
295: 
296: **Q:**If someone ambushes me in a battle at the Keep, when do my warriors get placed back in the Keep's clearing?
297: 
298: **A:**Immediately, as long as you spend a card. This means you can avoid the check for “no remaining warriors” prompted by the ambush.
299: 
300: 6.3Faction Setup
301: 
302: 6.3.1 Step 1: Gather Warriors and Wood.Form supplies of 25 warriors and 8 wood tokens.
303: 
304: 6.3.2 Step 2: Place Keep.Place the keep token in any corner clearing. This is your starting clearing.
305: 
306: 6.3.3 Step 3: Garrison.Place a warrior in each clearing except the clearing in the diagonally opposite corner from the clearing with the keep token.
307: 
308: 6.3.4 Step 4: Place Starting Buildings.Place 1 sawmill, 1 workshop, and 1 recruiter. You may place them among the clearing with the keep token and any adjacent clearings, in any combination.
309: 
310: 6.3.5 Step 5: Fill Buildings Tracks.Place your remaining 5 sawmills, 5 workshops, and 5 recruiters on the respective Buildings tracks from right to left. *(Leave the leftmost space of each track empty.)*
311: 
312: 6.4Birdsong
313: 
314: Place wood tokens in each clearing with any number of sawmills, one wood per sawmill there.
315: 
316: 6.5Daylight
317: 
318: First, you may activate workshops to craft cards from your hand. Then, you may take up to three actions—plus one action per bird card you spend *(not as part of an action)*—in any order and number.
319: 
320: 6.5.1 Battle.Initiate a battle.
321: 
322: 6.5.2 March.Take up to two moves.
323: 
324: 6.5.3 Recruit.Place one warrior at each recruiter. You may take this action only once per turn.
325: 
326: 6.5.4 Build.Place a building.
327: 
328: 1. Choose Clearing and Building.Choose a clearing you rule. Choose whether you want to place a sawmill, workshop, or recruiter. You will place the leftmost building of its type from your faction board. You must be able to pay its cost (6.5.4.II) and place it (6.5.4.III).
329: 2. Pay Cost.Find the chosen building's cost at the top of its column. Remove wood tokens equal in number to the cost from the chosen clearing, any adjacent clearings you rule, or any clearings connected to the chosen clearing you rule through any number of clearings you rule.
330: 3. Place Building and Score.Place the chosen building in the chosen clearing, and score the victory points listed on the space uncovered on your faction board.
331: 
332: 6.5.5 Overwork.Spend a card matching the clearing of a sawmill to place a wood token there.
333: 
334: 6.6Evening
335: 
336: Draw one card, plus one card per uncovered draw bonus. Then, if you have more than five cards in your hand, discard cards of your choice until you have five.
337: 
338: 7.Eyrie Dynasties
339: 
340: 7.1Overview
341: 
342: The Eyrie Dynasties wish to restore their once-dignified kind to their former glory in the Woodland by retaking control of the forest clearings. During their Evening, the Eyrie score victory points based on the number of roosts on the map. The greater their presence in the Woodland, the greater their gains. However, the Eyrie are bound by their Decree, an ever-increasing set of mandated actions promised by their leader. Each turn, they must take all of the actions on their Decree, or else fall into turmoil.
343: 
344: 7.2Faction Rules and Abilities
345: 
346: 7.2.1 Crafting.The Eyrie craft before resolving the Decree during Daylight by activating roosts.
347: 
348: 7.2.2 Lords of the Forest.The Eyrie rule a clearing when tied for most combined warriors and buildings there, and they have at least one Eyrie piece there.
349: 
350: 7.2.3 Disdain for Trade.Whenever the Eyrie craft an item, they ignore the listed victory points and instead score only one victory point. *(They can still score extra crafting points from effects such as Master Engravers and the Legendary Forge.)*
351: 
352: 7.3Faction Setup
353: 
354: 7.3.1 Step 1: Gather Warriors.Form a supply of 20 warriors.
355: 
356: 7.3.2 Step 2: Place Roost and Starting Warriors.Place 1 roost and 6 warriors in a corner clearing that is not the starting corner clearing of another player and, if possible, is diagonally opposite from a starting corner clearing. This is your starting clearing. *(This is updated from earlier printings for flexibility.)*
357: 
358: 7.3.3 Step 3: Choose Leader.Choose 1 of the 4 Eyrie leader cards and place it in your Leader Card slot. Gather the remaining leaders face up near you.
359: 
360: 7.3.4 Step 4: Tuck Viziers.Tuck your 2 Loyal Vizier cards, showing their suit, into the Decree columns above your faction board as listed on your leader.
361: 
362: 7.3.5 Step 5: Fill Roosts Track.Place your 6 remaining roosts on your Roosts track from right to left.
363: 
364: 7.4Birdsong
365: 
366: Your Birdsong has three steps in the following order.
367: 
368: 7.4.1 Emergency Orders.If you have no cards in your hand, draw one card.
369: 
370: 7.4.2 Add to the Decree.You must add one or two cards to the Decree, revealing them from your hand and tucking them, but only one card added may be a bird card. You may add each card to any column, and each column can hold any number of cards.
371: 
372: 7.4.3 A New Roost.If you have no roosts on the map, place a roost and three warriors in a clearing with the fewest warriors where all those pieces can be placed.
373: 
374: 7.5Daylight
375: 
376: Your Daylight has two steps in the following order.
377: 
378: 7.5.1 Craft.You may activate roosts to craft cards from your hand.
379: 
380: 7.5.2 Resolve the Decree.You must resolve the Decree, starting with the leftmost column and moving right. In each column, you must resolve all of its cards, but in any order. For each card, you must take the action listed for its column, as follows. If you cannot fully take an action, you immediately fall into turmoil (7.7).
381: 
382: **Q:**Can I move one warrior at a time from the same clearing to fulfill many Move cards in my Decree? Can I move the same warrior back and forth, given the right cards?
383: 
384: **A:**Yes! You can game the Decree as much as the cards allow you to. Just follow the rules for movement, and you're good.
385: 
386: 1. Recruit.Place a warrior in any clearing with a roost whose suit matches the card suit.
387: 2. Move.Move from any clearing whose suit matches the card suit. *(You must move at least one warrior.)*
388: 3. Battle.Initiate a battle in any clearing whose suit matches the card suit.
389: 4. Build.Place a roost in any clearing you rule whose suit matches the card suit and which has no roost.
390: 
391: 7.6Evening
392: 
393: Your Evening has two steps in the following order.
394: 
395: 7.6.1 Score Points.Score the victory points listed on the rightmost empty space of your Roosts track.
396: 
397: 7.6.2 Draw and Discard.Draw one card, plus one card per uncovered draw bonus. Then, if you have more than five cards in your hand, discard cards of your choice until you have five.
398: 
399: 7.7Turmoil
400: 
401: If you cannot fully take an action in the Decree (7.5.2) for any reason, you fall into turmoil. You must take the Turmoil action as follows in order.
402: 
403: **Q:**Does Turmoil trigger if I have an empty column?
404: 
405: **A:**Nope! Turmoil triggers if you have a card in your Decree that you can't complete.
406: 
407: **Q:**Does Turmoil trigger if I can take actions for some but not all cards in a column?
408: 
409: **A:**Yes! The moment you can't complete a single card, you go into Turmoil.
410: 
411: **Q:**If I have the Charismatic leader and Recruit, but I have one warrior left in my supply. Do I place no warriors or one warrior before going into Turmoil?
412: 
413: **A:**Place one. If you are prompted to place pieces but cannot place them all, you must place as many as possible.
414: 
415: 7.7.1 Step 1: Humiliate.Lose one victory point per bird card *(including Loyal Viziers)* on the Decree.
416: 
417: 7.7.2 Step 2: Purge.Discard all of the cards on the Decree except your Loyal Viziers.
418: 
419: 7.7.3 Step 3: Depose.Flip your current leader face down and set it aside, choose a new leader from those face up, and place on your faction board. Tuck your Loyal Viziers into the Decree spaces listed on your new leader.
420: 
421: 1. A New Clutch.If you must choose a new leader but none are face up, flip them all face up.
422: 
423: 7.7.4 Step 4: Rest.End Daylight and begin Evening.
424: 
425: 7.8Leaders Reference
426: 
427: The Eyrie have four leader cards, as follows.
428: 
429: 7.8.1 Builder.Loyal Viziers begin on Recruit and Move. Whenever you craft, you ignore your Disdain for Trade special ability (7.2.3).
430: 
431: 7.8.2 Charismatic.Loyal Viziers begin on Recruit and Battle. Whenever you take a Recruit action, you must place two warriors instead of one.
432: 
433: 7.8.3 Commander.Loyal Viziers begin on Move and Battle. In battle as attacker, you deal an extra hit.
434: 
435: **Q:**If I have the Charismatic leader and Recruit, but I have one warrior left in my supply. Do I place no warriors or one warrior before going into Turmoil?
436: 
437: **A:**Place one. If you are prompted to place pieces but cannot place them all, you must place as many as possible.
438: 
439: 7.8.4 Despot.Loyal Viziers begin on Move and Build. Whenever you remove at least one enemy building or token in battle, you score one extra victory point *(two in total, 3.2.1)*.
440: 
441: **Q:**What does the Despot's ability do? Don't I already get a victory point for removing a building or token?
442: 
443: **A:**Quite right you are! You get an extra point, though you do not get multiple extra points if you remove multiple buildings and/or tokens at the same time.
444: 
445: 8.Woodland Alliance
446: 
447: 8.1Overview
448: 
449: The Woodland Alliance works to gain the sympathy of the various creatures of the Woodland who are dissatisfied with their present condition. Each time the Alliance places a sympathy token, they may score victory points. The more sympathy on the map they have, the more victory points they score. Gaining the sympathy of the people requires supporters. These supporters can also be put toward violent ends, inciting outright rebellion across the forest. When a revolt erupts, the Alliance will establish a base. Bases allow the Alliance to train officers, increasing their military flexibility.
450: 
451: 8.2Faction Rules and Abilities
452: 
453: 8.2.1 Crafting.The Alliance crafts during Daylight by activating sympathy tokens.
454: 
455: 8.2.2 Guerrilla War.As defender in battle, the Alliance will deal hits equal to the higher roll, and the attacker will deal hits equal to the lower roll.
456: 
457: 8.2.3 The Supporters Stack.To take various actions, the Alliance spends supporters, which are cards on their Supporters stack. Supporters can only be spent for their suit and do not count against the Alliance's hand size. Supporters are face down, but the Alliance may inspect them at any time.
458: 
459: 1. Capacity.If the Alliance has no bases on the map, the Supporters stack can only hold up to five cards. If the Alliance would gain a supporter but the stack cannot hold it, that card is discarded. If any bases are on the map, the Supporters stack can hold unlimited cards.
460: 
461: 8.2.4 Removing Bases.Whenever a base is removed, the Alliance must discard all supporters matching the clearing of the base *(including birds)* and remove half of their officers, rounded up. If the Alliance has no more bases on the map and has more than five supporters, they must discard down to five supporters.
462: 
463: 8.2.5 Sympathy Tokens.The Alliance has 10 sympathy tokens.
464: 
465: **Q:**Does placing a piece in a sympathetic clearing trigger Outrage?
466: 
467: **A:**Nope! You have to move in warriors or remove the sympathy to trigger it.
468: 
469: 1. Placement Limits.A clearing can hold only one sympathy token.
470: 2. Terms.A sympathetic clearing is one with a sympathy token. An unsympathetic clearing is one without a sympathy token.
471: 
472: 8.2.6 Outrage.Whenever another player removes a sympathy token or moves any warriors into a sympathetic clearing, they must add one card matching the affected clearing from their hand to the Supporters stack. If they have no matching cards *(including no birds)*, they must show their hand to the Alliance, and then the Alliance draws a card from the deck and adds it to the Supporters stack.
473: 
474: **Q:**Does placing a piece in a sympathetic clearing trigger Outrage?
475: 
476: **A:**Nope! You have to move in warriors or remove the sympathy to trigger it.
477: 
478: **Q:**What happens if a hireling removes sympathy?
479: 
480: **A:**The player controlling the hireling would trigger Outrage, since Outrage specifies “When a player removes…” This is also covered explicitly in Not Found: H.3.7.
481: 
482: **Q:**Does the Vagabond cause Outrage?
483: 
484: **A:**Depends. Any player removing a sympathy token will cause outrage. Moving into a sympathetic clearing will not, as the Vagabond is a pawn, not a warrior.
485: 
486: **Q:**Do I trigger the Alliance's Outrage when I move into a sympathetic clearing?
487: 
488: **A:**Nope! You're a friendly Vagabond, and you have a pawn, not a warrior.
489: 
490: **Q:**If I move Allied warriors of the Woodland Alliance into a sympathetic clearing, do I trigger Outrage?
491: 
492: **A:**Nope! (\*This ruling was changed as of the release of the Marauder Expansion and the 8th Printing, because the Vagabond's Allied movement now uses the “Force” keyword.)
493: 
494: 8.3Faction Setup
495: 
496: 8.3.1 Step 1: Gather Warriors.Form a supply of 10 warriors.
497: 
498: 8.3.2 Step 2: Place Bases.Place 3 bases on the respective spaces in your Bases box.
499: 
500: 8.3.3 Step 3: Fill Sympathy Track.Place 10 sympathy tokens on your Sympathy track.
